header: Date: 2026-03-04 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42 mins | Attendees: Jordan Reyes (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Ethan Li (Redwood Partnerships); Liam O'Connor (CascadeCloud), Mei Chen (CascadeCloud), Dev Patel (CascadeCloud)
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and CascadeCloud. Discussed integration touchpoints (marketplace vs reseller), technical hosting options (hosted API, Dedicated pools, Private VPC/on-prem), security/compliance needs (SOC2, audit logs, KMS), and mutual GTM motions. Agreed next steps: share partner 1-pager, security docs, schedule SE deep dive and exchange infra diagrams.
transcript: 00:00 - Jordan Reyes: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Jordan from Redwood on the AE side, with Priya our SE and Ethan from partnerships. How's everyone?
00:08 - Liam O'Connor: Good thanks, Liam here. Excited to learn more about Redwood and see where CascadeCloud and Redwood might partner up.
00:14 - Mei Chen: Hi all, Mei here. We're particularly curious about private deployments and how Redwood could fit into our marketplace offering.

00:20 - Jordan Reyes: Great â€” high level, Redwood's a developer-first inference platform. We do hosted API, reserved dedicated capacity, and private VPC/on-prem installs. Today we'd like to understand CascadeCloud's goals, tech constraints, and GTM model. Priya, want to add?

00:30 - Priya Shah: Yeah, hi. I'll listen for infra details and note what a tech deep dive should cover â€” things like model compatibility, latency expectations, and networking (VPC peering, transit, etc.).

00:45 - Dev Patel: Quick context: CascadeCloud is expanding marketplace offerings for managed ML infra. We want partners that can be deployed into customer VPCs and also provide a resellable managed service. Key constraints: tenant isolation, encryption at rest with customer KMS, and regional data residency for EU customers.

01:10 - Jordan Reyes: Makes sense. For private deployments we do a control plane that can be customer-managed, and the inference nodes can live in their VPC. KMS/HSM integrations are supported. On residency, we have region-aware routing. We should follow up with our security doc but high-level we support bring-your-own-KMS and audit logs.
01:35 - Mei Chen: How heavy is the install? Our ops teams care about upgrade automation and air-gapped installs for some regulated customers.

01:45 - Priya Shah: We have an on-prem installer option that can run air-gapped; upgrades are orchestrated via our private channel. For Dedicated (hosted reserved), it's fully managed by Redwood but you can get SLA and dedicated GPU pools. For marketplace/reseller, there's multiple modes â€” we can support an image/containerized package or a SaaS integration.

02:10 - Liam O'Connor: On commercial side, we're thinking reseller model where CascadeCloud sells Redwood Dedicated as part of our managed ML offering. Curious about pricing structure and whether there's partner margin.

02:20 - Ethan Li: We have partner programs; Jordan can share partner 1-pager with pricing frameworks. There's both revenue share and referral models depending on level of support and co-managed operations.

02:35 - Dev Patel: On technical perf: typical customers run 7B/13B models and some larger 70B. Our expectation: sub-200ms token latency for interactive apps and decent throughput for batch jobs. How does Redwood handle quantization and batching?

02:55 - Priya Shah: Redwood runtime is GPU-optimized and supports quantized execution paths. We do smart batching and prefix/KV caching to reduce per-token cost. For the 70B family, latency depends on instance types and KV cache locality; we often recommend model variants or quantization to hit sub-200ms for short contexts. That said, interactive SLOs can be met in Dedicated setups with the right GPU configs.
03:30 - Dev Patel: When you say KV cache locality â€” do you mean cache within the same node or across nodes? We worry about cross-node hops adding latency.

03:40 - Priya Shah: Good question â€” cache is kept local to the serving instance; we avoid cross-node KV fetches during generation. Smart routing helps keep sessions pinned to nodes with warm cache. There are tradeoffs with autoscaling, but we can tune policies.
04:05 - Mei Chen: Security: SOC2 is a must for many of our enterprise customers. Do you have SOC2 reports or ISO? Also SSO/SAML for admin console?

04:15 - Jordan Reyes: We are SOC2 Type II and have ISO underway; I'll attach the cert in the follow-up. RBAC and SAML/SSO are available for the console; audit logs can be exported. We do per-tenant encryption keys too.
04:35 - Liam O'Connor: Great. On integration surface, what APIs would we point to for a marketplace offer â€” redirect to hosted API endpoints or call Dedicated endpoints?

04:45 - Priya Shah: Both possible. For a fully managed marketplace listing, redirecting to our hosted API is simplest. For co-managed or resold capacity, we provision Dedicated capacity reserved for CascadeCloud and expose endpoints that you can front through your control plane.
05:05 - Dev Patel: Network-wise, can we do VPC peering and private link type connections? Some customers won't allow public endpoints.
05:15 - Jordan Reyes: Yes â€” we support VPC peering and private links. For on-prem or air-gapped customers, we also have an offline package though that requires some ops collaboration.

05:35 - Mei Chen: A few customer scenarios: 1) Startup using Redwood hosted API via our marketplace, 2) Enterprise wanting Dedicated within CascadeCloud's region with KMS keys, 3) Regulated customer needing on-prem. Do you handle all three?

05:50 - Priya Shah: Yes â€” we've seen that spread. Hosted API is easiest for startups, Dedicated for enterprise/reseller setups, and Private/on-prem for highly regulated. Each has different provisioning lead times.
06:10 - Liam O'Connor: Lead times â€” what are we talking for Dedicated vs Private?
06:15 - Jordan Reyes: Dedicated: typically 2-4 weeks depending on reserved capacity and region. Private/on-prem: depends on network and security review, often 4-8 weeks with standard integrations.
06:30 - Dev Patel: For benchmarking, can we run a POC to validate latency and throughput on our infra? We can provide sample models and traffic patterns.

06:40 - Priya Shah: Absolutely. We often do a POC where we run a benchmark harness against a Dedicated pool or a private deployment. We'll need perf targets, model list, and dataset sample; then we can run cost/latency profiles.
07:00 - Mei Chen: On billing, how granular is usage reporting? Our marketplace customers want token-level costs and per-route dashboards.
07:08 - Jordan Reyes: Redwood Console provides token-level cost breakdowns, per-model dashboards, traces, and route-level metrics. We can also export raw usage for billing reconciliation.
07:25 - Liam O'Connor: Any constraints around models â€” can customers bring their own models or only curated catalog?

07:33 - Priya Shah: We support a curated catalog as well as customer model onboarding for Private and Dedicated. Hosted catalog is curated for quality and performance but we can evaluate custom models for Dedicated/private installs.
07:50 - Dev Patel: Network security again â€” do you support customer-managed bastion or must it connect to Redwood control plane? We have strict egress rules.

07:58 - Jordan Reyes: For Private installs, the control plane can be a customer-managed instance or we can run it in a private tenancy. We support tightened egress; in extreme cases we support fully offline setups.
08:15 - Mei Chen: On API features: function/tool calling and streaming â€” important for some partners. Do those work over Private/Dedicated installs?
08:25 - Priya Shah: Yes, streaming and function/tool calling are supported across modes. There are nuances for tool integrations in air-gapped environments but core functionality is the same.
08:40 - Liam O'Connor: A naive question â€” how do you handle model fallbacks? If a region runs out of capacity do you route to a different variant?

08:50 - Jordan Reyes: Smart routing can fallback to compatible model variants or another region based on policy, maintaining SLA tradeoffs. We expose routing controls to partners so you can prioritize latency, cost, or regional residency.
09:10 - Dev Patel: Great. For marketplace integration, we might want a white-label flow where customers see CascadeCloud branding but the underlying service is Redwood. Is that supported?
09:18 - Ethan Li: We can discuss white-label options in the partner program. There's technical and commercial terms but we've done co-branded flows before.
09:30 - Mei Chen: About quotas and rate limits â€” can we set per-tenant quotas from the CascadeCloud side for customers who buy through our marketplace?
09:38 - Priya Shah: Yes, we have per-tenant quotas and rate limiting. You can set quotas via the partner console or via API depending on the integration type.
09:50 - Liam O'Connor: On the legal/compliance side, customers ask for data residency and retention policies. How granular are retention controls?
09:58 - Jordan Reyes: We allow configurable retention policies and per-customer opt-outs. For Private, data never leaves the customer's environment unless you opt into metrics export.
10:10 - Dev Patel: For the POC, what do you need from our side? We'll try to scope a bench that tests 13B and 70B with both chat and embeddings workloads.

10:20 - Priya Shah: We'll need: 1) model list and version, 2) sample inference payloads and concurrency patterns, 3) perf targets (p99 latency, throughput), 4) networking details for where tests will run. We'll package a benchmark harness and run with you.
10:40 - Mei Chen: Any constraints on GPU vendors? Our infra is mixed â€” some A100 hosts, some newer H100 capacity. Do you support both?
10:48 - Priya Shah: Yes â€” runtime supports NVIDIA A100 and H100 and we tune kernels accordingly. For H100 we can generally get better perf/latency but cost profiles differ.
11:05 - Liam O'Connor: Customers sometimes ask about model quantization â€” do you help with quantization profiles?
11:12 - Priya Shah: Redwood Optimize provides recommendations on quantization and batching per workload; we can run a quick eval to recommend a quantization profile that balances quality vs cost.
11:30 - Dev Patel: We also need clarity on logging vs PII â€” if we log requests for observability, is that sanitized?
11:38 - Jordan Reyes: We configurable mask PII and provide redaction options. Audit logs can be configured not to include user payloads if required.
11:55 - Mei Chen: What's the typical revenue share for reseller partners? Not a hard number now, just a ballpark.

12:02 - Ethan Li: Ballpark depends on commitment and co-support. Referral deals might be 10-20% while co-managed reseller margins can go higher depending on volume and SLAs. We'll share partner program doc.
12:20 - Liam O'Connor: Sounds reasonable. On the go-to-market, we want co-marketing and joint webinars for launch. Is that in your usual partner playbook?
12:28 - Jordan Reyes: Yes â€” we do joint webinars, case studies, and co-marketing credits for launch partners.
12:40 - Dev Patel: One last infra nit: for multi-tenant Dedicated, is there strict tenant isolation or just namespace separation?

12:48 - Priya Shah: Dedicated provides pooled GPU capacity reserved for a partner and we can enforce tenant isolation at the runtime level; for the highest isolation we recommend Private where you get dedicated nodes per tenant or per customer as needed.
13:10 - Mei Chen: OK great. I think we have enough to plan next steps. Can we recap?

13:18 - Jordan Reyes: Recap: Jordan will send partner one-pager, pricing framework, and SOC2 summary. Priya will prepare technical slides and propose deep-dive agenda. Dev will share infra diagrams and perf targets. We schedule an SE deep dive week of 2026-03-09. Agreed?
13:40 - Liam O'Connor: Agreed.
13:44 - Dev Patel: Agreed, will send diagrams by 2026-03-09.
13:48 - Mei Chen: Thanks all, look forward to the POC.
13:52 - Jordan Reyes: Thanks everyone â€” we'll follow up via email with the items. Meeting adjourned.
